DAMOCLES fits over many configurations of regimes or covariates

Source: R/damocles_configurations.R
damocles_samples.Rd

damocles_samples() fits damocles_fit(), with parameters shared by all communities, once for each configuration in a list of regimes or of edge_covariate, and compares each fit with constant rates by damocles_lrt(). The configurations are typically samples from the posterior distribution of a method that estimates rates of diversification along the tree, so that the uncertainty in where rates shift, or in branch-specific rates, carries over to the conclusions about local colonisation and extinction instead of resting on a single configuration.

Usage

damocles_samples(
  comm,
  tree,
  regimes = NULL,
  edge_covariate = NULL,
  vary = c("both", "gamma", "mu"),
  root = c("both", "absent", "present"),
  sympatry = 0,
  cores = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'mc_damocles_samples'
summary(object, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), ...)

Arguments

comm

Presences of the species (columns, named as the tips of tree) in one or more communities (rows): a matrix or data frame, or a named vector for one community. Values above zero count as presences. Tips missing from comm count as absent, with a warning, and species of comm missing from the tree are dropped.

tree

A rooted, fully dichotomous phylo tree with branch lengths.

regimes, edge_covariate

A list of configurations, each a vector with one value per edge of tree in the order of tree$edge (see damocles_fit()). Give one of the two.

vary

Which rates change among regimes or with edge_covariate: "both", "gamma" or "mu"; the other one is a single rate for the whole tree.

root

Prior on the state of the ancestor at the root: "both", "absent" or "present".

sympatry

In damocles_loglik(), the probability that a present ancestor leaves both daughters present (see simulate_damocles()). In damocles_fit(), a fixed value, or NULL to estimate it with the rates (shared or not, as they are).

cores

Number of cores, with configurations fitted in parallel. Not available on Windows, where one core is used.

object

A result of damocles_samples().

probs

Probabilities of the quantiles.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class mc_damocles_samples with samples, a data frame with one row per configuration (n_par, loglik, delta_aic against constant rates, and the likelihood-ratio statistic, df and p_value), constant, the fit with constant rates, fits, the fit of each configuration, and gamma and mu, matrices of the rate of each edge (rows) in each configuration (columns).

Details

With BAMM output read by BAMMtools::getEventData(), for example, the regimes of sample i are factor(edata$eventVectors[[i]]) and the mean branch rates of speciation are the columns of BAMMtools::getMarginalBranchRateMatrix(edata)$lambda_branch_matrix, both in the order of tree$edge when edata was built on tree (data-raw/damocles_bamm.R shows the whole path). With ClaDS (RPANDA::fit_ClaDS()), the branch rates of one posterior sample are exp(l_0 + alpha * sampler$alpha_effect + x), where l_0, alpha and the values x of the edges are columns of the chains, transformed as in RPANDA::getMAPS_ClaDS() (data-raw/damocles_clads.R). Any other method works the same way once its output is a vector per edge; dr_rates() gives one from the tree alone.

Configurations of regimes and of continuous rates behave differently. A posterior sample of regimes is one plausible partition, and the spread of the fits across samples shows how much the conclusions depend on where the shifts are. A posterior sample of branch rates also carries the sampling noise of each rate, and a noisy covariate attenuates its slope (regression dilution): in data-raw/damocles_clads.R, with colonisation simulated from the MAP rates of ClaDS with beta = 2, the MAP rates gave a slope of 1.6 and rejected constant rates, while single posterior samples gave a median slope of 0.22 and rejected constant rates in 65 of 100. For continuous rates, fit the posterior mean, median or MAP of each rate with damocles_fit() for the estimate, and use the posterior samples to see whether the sign and the comparison with constant rates hold, knowing that each sample understates the slope.

summary() reports, across configurations, how often the varying rates fit better than constant rates (p-value below 0.05, and AIC lower by more than 2), quantiles of the parameters that mean the same in every fit (such as mu when only gamma varies, or beta_gamma), and quantiles of the rate of each edge, which are comparable whatever the regimes of each sample. Regimes differ among posterior samples, so the parameters of each regime are only comparable within a sample.

The configurations are only as good as the method that produced them. The reliability of the rate shifts inferred by BAMM has been debated (Moore et al. 2016; Rabosky et al. 2017); comparing several sources of regimes, including partitions defined a priori with clade_regimes(), and testing a configuration against random partitions with damocles_partition_test() guard against relying on one of them.

References

Moore, B. R., Höhna, S., May, M. R., Rannala, B., & Huelsenbeck, J. P. (2016). Critically evaluating the theory and performance of Bayesian analysis of macroevolutionary mixtures. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 113, 9569–9574. doi:10.1073/pnas.1518659113

Rabosky, D. L., Mitchell, J. S., & Chang, J. (2017). Is BAMM flawed? Theoretical and practical concerns in the analysis of multi-rate diversification models. Systematic Biology, 66, 477–498. doi:10.1093/sysbio/syx037

See also

damocles_fit(), damocles_lrt(), damocles_partition_test().

Examples

set.seed(7)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(30)
crown <- ape::Ntip(tr) + 2
comm <- simulate_damocles(tr, ifelse(clade_regimes(tr, list(A = crown)) == "A", 3, 0.5),
                          mu = 1, n = 5)
# three configurations, as if sampled from a posterior
configurations <- lapply(c(crown, crown + 1, crown + 2), function(node) {
  clade_regimes(tr, list(A = node))
})
res <- damocles_samples(comm, tr, regimes = configurations, vary = "gamma")
res
#> DAMOCLES fits over 3 configurations, parameters shared by 5 communities
#> Better than constant rates: p < 0.05 in 1 and AIC lower by more than 2 in 1 of 3 
summary(res)
#> DAMOCLES fits over 3 configurations
#> 
#> Proportion of configurations better than constant rates:
#>         measure proportion
#>  p_value < 0.05      0.333
#>  delta_aic < -2      0.333
#> 
#> Likelihood-ratio statistic:
#>   5%  50%  95% 
#> 1.68 3.35 5.72 
#> Difference in AIC (varying - constant):
#>     5%    50%    95% 
#> -3.718 -1.352  0.323 
#> 
#> Parameters shared by every fit:
#>          5%     50%  95%
#> mu 1.88e-09 4.6e-09 3.05
#> 
#> Rates of each edge: see `$edges`
